decision.reason: Four-warp padded whole-row remains faster than both controls through M42. M1 remains slower for every warp count, and RCCL makes unfused faster from M43.

M1_stage_decomposition_us_per_site.explanation: At M1 the single triton CTA does not expose enough independent remote-load work. Its no-sync padded core is 8.95 us slower than the Iris fused core. Triton's omitted exit barrier recovers part of that loss but cannot overcome it. Prefix-copy marginals varied across cumulative graphs and are not used for this attribution.

M2_stage_decomposition_us_per_site.explanation: The second row launches a second CTA, allowing triton-shmem to overlap remote-load latency; the core falls from 15.95 us at M1 to 6.19 us at M2.

M1_dynamic_specialization_fix.full_model_sanity: A TP4 GLM server was bounded to five minutes and stopped at 62% checkpoint loading before readiness. No request was issued.
M1_dynamic_specialization_fix.profile_policy: Keep M1 ordinary fallback until the dynamic kernel is measured at qualified WS8.

retained_incidents: The first exact-profile M42 graph run entered a high-tail performance mode (90.89 us p50); an isolated retry measured 39.34 us p50. Both artifacts are retained.
The eight-warp padded M192 run remained active without progress and was terminated; four warps was already the winner and M192 was outside the profitable region.
